_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 6: Classification Rules for High-Risk AI Systems
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. No harmonised standard is requested for Article 6 classification. Article 6(5) requires Commission guidelines with practical examples. The Commission published draft guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems on 19 May 2026.
basis: EU AI Act Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation)
EU AI Act Annex III (High-risk AI systems)
EU AI Act Article 6(3) exception criteria
Draft Commission guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems (published 19 May 2026; Art. 6(5))
_metadata.awaiting_standard: No harmonised standard is requested for Article 6 classification. Article 6(5) requires Commission guidelines with practical examples. The Commission published draft guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems on 19 May 2026.

step_1.question: Does the AI system satisfy Art. 6(1)(a) — i.e. is it intended to be used as a safety component, interpreted in accordance with Art. 3(14) and Art. 6(1a)-(1b), of a product covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, or is it itself such a product — AND does it also satisfy Art. 6(1)(b), meaning that the relevant product is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment under that legislation? Apply Art. 6(1c): an assessment required solely because of risks other than risks to health and safety does not meet point (b).

step_2.question: Does the AI system fall under one of the use-case categories listed in Annex III?
step_2.if_no: NOT HIGH-RISK under Art. 6 — may still be subject to other AI Act provisions (e.g., Art. 50 transparency obligations for certain AI systems)

step_3.question: Does the Art. 6(3) derogation apply? An AI system referred to in Annex III is not considered high-risk where it 'does not pose a significant risk of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights of natural persons, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision making' and at least one of the following conditions is fulfilled: (a) it is intended to perform a narrow procedural task; (b) it is intended to improve the result of a previously completed human activity; (c) it is intended to detect decision-making patterns or deviations from prior decision-making patterns and is not meant to replace or influence the previously completed human assessment, without proper human review; (d) it is intended to perform a preparatory task to an assessment relevant for the purposes of the use cases listed in Annex III. The derogation never applies where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons: such a system 'shall always be considered to be high-risk' (Art. 6(3), third subparagraph).
step_3.if_yes: NOT HIGH-RISK (Art. 6(3) exception) — the provider MUST document its assessment before the system is placed on the market or put into service, MUST register itself and the system in the EU database (Art. 49(2)) and MUST provide the documentation to national competent authorities upon request (Art. 6(4))
step_3.if_no: HIGH-RISK via Art. 6(2) — subject to the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 (Arts. 8-15)

Section A — In vitro diagnostic medical devices (Regulation (EU) 2017/746)

annex_iii_categories.description: Remote biometric identification systems, biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes or characteristics, and emotion recognition, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law (Annex III, point 1)
subcategories: Remote biometric identification systems, wherever used; biometric verification the sole purpose of which is to confirm that a specific natural person is the person he or she claims to be is excluded (point 1(a))

Biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes or characteristics based on the inference of those attributes or characteristics (point 1(b)); categorising individual natural persons to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation is prohibited under Art. 5(1)(g), subject to the exceptions stated there

Emotion recognition systems (point 1(c)); inferring emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions is prohibited under Art. 5(1)(f), except where the system is intended for medical or safety reasons

annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems intended as safety components in the management and operation of critical infrastructure
subcategories: Road traffic management
Water supply
Gas supply
Heating supply
Electricity supply
Critical digital infrastructure

annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems that determine access to or affect progression in education and vocational training
subcategories: Access or admission decisions
Assignment to institutions or programs

Evaluation of learning outcomes, including when those outcomes are used to steer the learning process (point 3(b)); assessment of the appropriate level of education that an individual will receive or will be able to access (point 3(c))
Monitoring and detection of prohibited behaviour during exams (cheating detection)

annex_iii_categories.category: Employment, workers management and access to self-employment
annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems used in recruitment, selection, and management of workers
subcategories: Recruitment and selection (CV screening, interview evaluation)

Decisions affecting terms of work-related relationships, promotion or termination of work-related contractual relationships; allocation of tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits or characteristics (point 4(b))
Monitoring and evaluation of worker performance and behaviour

annex_iii_categories.category: Access to essential private services and public services and benefits
annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems evaluating eligibility for essential services
subcategories: Evaluation of the creditworthiness of natural persons or establishment of their credit score, except AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud (point 5(b))
Risk assessment and pricing for life/health insurance

Evaluation, by or on behalf of public authorities, of the eligibility of natural persons for essential public assistance benefits and services, including healthcare services, and granting, reducing, revoking or reclaiming them (point 5(a))
Evaluation and classification of emergency calls by natural persons; dispatching, or establishing priority in the dispatching of, emergency first response services (point 5(d))
Emergency healthcare patient triage systems (point 5(d))

annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law (Annex III, point 6)
subcategories: Assessment of the risk of a natural person becoming the victim of criminal offences (point 6(a))
Polygraph and similar tools
Evaluation of reliability of evidence

Assessment of the risk of a natural person offending or re-offending not solely on the basis of profiling, or assessment of personality traits and characteristics or past criminal behaviour of natural persons or groups (point 6(d)); risk assessments predicting a criminal offence based solely on profiling or on assessing personality traits and characteristics are prohibited under Art. 5(1)(d), which does not apply to AI systems used to support the human assessment of the involvement of a person in a criminal activity, which is already based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity
Profiling of natural persons in criminal investigations
Not in the adopted Annex III: crime analytics on large data sets (a Commission-proposal item); such a system is high-risk only where it falls under one of points 6(a) to 6(e)

annex_iii_categories.category: Migration, asylum and border control management
annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems used in migration and border control
subcategories: Risk assessment for security, irregular migration, or health risks
Examination of applications for asylum, visa, and residence permits
Detecting, recognising or identifying natural persons in the context of migration, asylum or border control management, with the exception of the verification of travel documents (point 7(d))
Polygraphs or similar tools (point 7(a))

annex_iii_categories.category: Administration of justice and democratic processes
annex_iii_categories.description: AI systems assisting judicial authorities or used in democratic processes
subcategories: Research and interpretation of facts and law, application of law to facts
Alternative dispute resolution

Influencing the outcome of an election or referendum or the voting behaviour of natural persons, excluding AI systems to the output of which natural persons are not directly exposed, such as tools used to organise, optimise or structure political campaigns from an administrative or logistical point of view (point 8(b))

art6_3_exception_criteria.description: An AI system referred to in Annex III is NOT high-risk where it does not pose a significant risk of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights of natural persons, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision making, AND at least one of these conditions is fulfilled. The derogation never applies where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons (Art. 6(3), third subparagraph):

criteria.label: Narrow procedural task
criteria.description: The system performs a narrow procedural task (e.g., converting unstructured data to structured, document classification for filing)

criteria.label: Improvement of prior human activity
criteria.description: The system improves the result of a previously completed human activity (e.g., grammar check on a human-written decision)

criteria.label: Pattern detection without replacement
criteria.description: The system is intended to detect decision-making patterns or deviations from prior decision-making patterns and is not meant to replace or influence the previously completed human assessment, without proper human review (e.g., flagging inconsistencies for human review)

criteria.label: Preparatory task
criteria.description: The system performs a preparatory task to an assessment relevant for the purposes of the use cases listed in Annex III (e.g., data preprocessing before a human makes the actual decision)

art6_3_exception_criteria.documentation_requirement: The provider MUST document its assessment before the system is placed on the market or put into service, and MUST provide the documentation of the assessment upon request of national competent authorities (Art. 6(4)). Before placing the system on the market or putting it into service, the provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative MUST register itself and the system in the EU database referred to in Art. 71 (Art. 6(4) and Art. 49(2)). The Regulation requires no notification to a national authority.

scoring.high_risk_art6_1: System is a safety component of, or itself, a product under Annex I legislation and that product is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment (Art. 6(1), (1a)-(1c)) — HIGH-RISK
scoring.high_risk_art6_2: System falls under Annex III and Art. 6(3) exception does NOT apply — HIGH-RISK
scoring.not_high_risk_exception: System falls under Annex III but Art. 6(3) exception applies — NOT HIGH-RISK (must document the assessment and register under Art. 49(2))
scoring.not_high_risk: System does not meet both conditions of Art. 6(1) and does not fall under an Annex III use case — NOT HIGH-RISK under Art. 6
scoring.unable_to_determine: Insufficient information to classify — manual review required
